## Summary

**Re-scoped** follow-up to the completed twin **WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO** (shipped in
v1.0.13, commit `9e8ca646`, epic WL-0MTFNII4X00632CG), which already delivered this
item's original AC1–AC3 (the unbounded same-timestamp conflict loop and the
unattributed-soft-delete override). Those are now shipped; this item is narrowed to the
**residual** that the earlier fix left in place.

**Residual defect:** `mergeSameTimestampItems` still writes a **fresh wall-clock
`updatedAt`** whenever a non-`sortIndex` field is reconciled and the merged result
differs from local (`src/sync.ts` ~L833):

```ts
if (nonSortIndexMerged && !mergedEqualsLocal) {
  merged.updatedAt = new Date().toISOString();   // <-- wall-clock stamp on a merge
}
```

A merge is not a user edit. Stamping "now" silently re-timestamps audit-fresh items and
marks valid audits stale, and it feeds further timestamp churn on subsequent syncs.

## Problem

Observed on 2026-09-21: a single sync (`18:35:58 → 18:36:17`) logged **244 conflicts**
and re-timestamped **95 items** to `2026-09-21T18:36:06` (48 of them `completed`).
**14 `completed`/`in_review` items lost audit freshness purely from merge churn** — e.g.
*Sync: regression guard…* (`WL-0MSOYWZTH003JFVD`) was audited 2026-08-31, had no activity
since, yet became "stale" because the merge moved `updatedAt`.

Because `updatedAt` underpins `isAuditFresh` (until the content-fingerprint gate lands,
P1), merge churn drives false staleness → redundant downtime re-audits → more writes →
more churn.

## Expected behaviour

- A merge must **never** introduce a wall-clock `updatedAt`. A same-timestamp merge
  inherits an existing timestamp (the two sides are equal by definition), so repeated
  syncs of the same divergence are **quiescent**.
- Merged content still converges on both sides.
- Audit freshness is unaffected by a merge that did not change user-authored content.

## Acceptance criteria

- AC1: `mergeSameTimestampItems` no longer calls `new Date().toISOString()` for
  `updatedAt`; the merged item inherits the (equal) existing timestamp.
- AC2: Regression test: two divergent copies with the same `updatedAt` (differing in one
  non-`sortIndex` field) merged repeatedly are quiescent — `updatedAt` never advances and
  content converges.
- AC3: Regression test: a same-timestamp conflict resolved to remote content leaves
  `updatedAt` unchanged and `isAuditFresh(auditedAt, updatedAt)` true for a prior valid
  audit.
- AC4: `mergeDifferentTimestampItems` continues to inherit the winning side's timestamp
  (no wall-clock); an explicit assertion is added.
- AC5: Full existing test suite passes, including the sync convergence + delete-protection
  tests shipped under WL-0MTFNII4X00632CG.

## Notes / open questions

- The original bump existed so the merged side would be unambiguously "newer" on the next
  sync. With both sides writing the merged result, convergence should hold without it;
  confirm via the AC2 quiescence test.
- A same-timestamp `sortIndex`-only conflict already never bumps (unchanged).

## References

- discovered-from: WL-0MSIAOFI70075REE
- shipped predecessor (do not re-implement): WL-0MSKZ30SK007K9TO (completed/done,
  v1.0.13, `9e8ca646`), WL-0MTFNII4X00632CG, WL-0MT2KZH0I005XUWE
- related-to: WL-0MUBVH5S0008NQ9K (P1 — content-fingerprint freshness gate)
- evidence: `.worklog/logs/sync.log` (2026-09-21T18:35:58 → 18:36:17)
data.title: Sync merges must not re-timestamp audit-fresh items (remove wall-clock updatedAt bump)

data.description:
# Make the downtime owner-lease gate per-slot

Parent RCA: WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28.

## Goal

In cheap mode (3 slots) the downtime dispatcher must keep dispatching into **unowned free slots**
even while another dispatched agent holds the shared local-dispatch lease. Today it dispatches
nothing for the whole duration of any agent run, wasting 2–3 slots.

## Problem

`packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` `tick()` applies a **machine-wide** gate before reading the
coordination file:

```ts
const ownerLeaseHeld = /* local_owner_session_id string OR local_owner_lease_remaining_seconds > 0 */;
const slotOwned = ownerLeaseHeld && (runningPanes ?? 0) > 0;
if (slotOwned) return { polled: true, dispatched: false, idle: true };
```

There is no per-slot branch — it fires even when `requiredFreeSlots < total_slots` (per-slot mode).
So a single working agent that holds a lease blocks all dispatch, despite `countFreeUnownedSlots`
reporting free slots. Evidence: proxy UTC 00:01–00:12, cheap mode, `total_slots=3`,
`available_slots=2`, lease held by a dispatched pane, **zero dispatches**.

The gate's comment claims it is only the count-based (single-slot) fallback and is superseded by
per-slot identity. That is not what the code does.

## Required behaviour

- Detect per-slot mode from the status (`Array.isArray(status.slots)` and a usable slot array).
- In per-slot mode, allow dispatch while `countFreeUnownedSlots(status.slots) >= <tier minimum>`;
  the global owner lease must not block dispatch into free unowned slots.
- Keep the conservative gate only for the count-based (single-slot / no per-slot data) path, so a
  truly owned sole slot is still protected.
- Never dispatch into a slot whose per-slot `owner_session_id` is set.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Unit test: per-slot status with 3 slots, 1 owned/busy and 2 free unowned, a held global lease,
   and `runningPanes > 0` → dispatch **proceeds** (regression test for this RCA).
2. Unit test: count-based status (no `slots`), `local_lease_active`/owner held, `runningPanes > 0`
   → dispatch is **refused** (single-slot protection preserved).
3. Unit test: per-slot status where every slot is owned → dispatch refused.
4. Audit-tier minimum (`DOWNTIME_AUDIT_MIN_FREE_SLOTS = 2`) is evaluated against the per-slot
   unowned-free count.
5. Integration/manual evidence: in cheap mode, dispatches are observed in `downtime-dispatches.log`
   while a previously dispatched agent is still `working`.

## Notes

- `countFreeUnownedSlots` and `isSlotOwned` already exist and exclude owned slots.
- Do not weaken the single-slot path: an owned sole slot must still block.
data.title: Downtime dispatcher: owner-lease gate must be per-slot (slotOwned blocks dispatch despite free slots)

discovered-from: WL-0MU8807BI008C9ME

## Problem

The report skill (`~/.pi/agent/skills/report/scripts/render_report.py`) renders `Audit: ❔ not run` for items whose audit IS persisted and passing.

Root cause: `_fetch_work_item` reads `data.get('workItem', {})` and then `work_item.get('auditResult')` (line ~235). Since the Worklog migration, `wl show <id> --json` exposes the structured audit at the TOP LEVEL (`result.auditResult` — an object with `readyToClose`, `auditedAt`), while `workItem.auditResult` is the legacy field and is always null. The renderer expects a boolean, so it always falls through to 'not run'.

Observed on WL-0MU8807BI008C9ME: `wl show --json` top-level auditResult={readyToClose:true}, but the rendered report said 'Audit: not run'.

## Fix

Read the top-level `auditResult` object and map `readyToClose` -> passed/failed; fall back to the legacy boolean if present.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A passing persisted audit renders `Audit: passed`.
2. A `readyToClose:false` audit renders `Audit: failed`.
3. An item with no audit renders `Audit: not run`.
data.title: report skill: audit verdict shows 'not run' because it reads legacy workItem.auditResult

data.description: Right now we can enter ship mode even if there is work underway in another agent. We need to prevent this happening. Scan all workspaces for work that is ongoing in the project we are trying to ship. If any pane relates to the project being shipped then inform the user they cannot enter ship mode until work has been completed and panes have been closed. This should happen before the confirmation dialog is shown. If the confirmation dialog is shown and the user types 'ship' then the project should immediately be placed in code freeze.
data.title: Do not enter ship mode if work is in progress, place in code freeze the moment we enter ship mode

Gap fixes pushed to dev (commit 2dfb909b), addressing the audit's two partial ACs:

- AC3: the all-owned fixture had slot-3 free+unowned (countFreeUnownedSlots=1), so refusal came from the requiredFreeSlots gate, not the all-owned condition. Fixed the fixture so every slot carries an owner_session_id (countFreeUnownedSlots=0) and added a direct countFreeUnownedSlots all-owned assertion.
- AC5: added a cheap-mode integration test that drives the real worker tick with a previously dispatched agent still working (runningPanes>0 + held owner lease) and asserts the dispatch marker is written to .worklog/downtime-dispatches.log via the real appendDowntimeLogEntry.

Full suite green at commit 2dfb909b (643 herdr tests; full monorepo gate passed in implement.py finish).
